sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by non-permeabilized anti-S-protein immunocytochemistry in CHO cells (L7) and by luminal-surface antibody binding in perfused mouse hearts (L4) and immunofluorescence confocal microscopy of capillary cross-sections (L5). LPL-binding function of the S-tagged construct is NOT MEASURED explicitly in the provided clips (though the comparison construct GPIHBP1-W109S is noted as LPL-binding-deficient, implying WT S-GPIHBP1 retains binding).
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly names residues 32–48 as the replaced region, placing the tag junction after residue 31 (E) in canonical UniProt numbering; Python confirms seq[30]='E' and seq[31]='D'. GPIHBP1 is GPI-anchored with no TM helix, so residues 21–184 are entirely extracellular and there is no TM-proximity constraint. The acidic domain (residues 32–48) is a disordered, low-complexity stretch well-suited to tag replacement, and L4/L5/L7 confirm the tagged protein reaches the cell surface in both mouse endothelium and transfected CHO cells. Full-length GPI-anchored GPIHBP1 construct in which residues 32–48 (the acidic domain including the sulfated tyrosine) were replaced with the 15-aa S-protein tag (KETAAAKFERQHMDS). Expressed in CHO pgsA-745 cells (L6/L7) and knocked into the mouse Gpihbp1 locus by CRISPR/Cas9 (L2/L3). Non-permeabilized immunocytochemistry (L7) and intravascular antibody perfusion of mouse hearts (L4) confirmed tag accessibility on the extracellular/luminal surface.

sources.claim: A vector for S-GPIHBP1 was generated by replacing sequences for GPIHBP1 residues 32 to 48 with sequences for the S-protein tag.

literature_notes: All seven ledger lines converge on a single site: the S-protein tag replacing the acidic domain (residues 32–48) of full-length GPI-anchored GPIHBP1. L1 provides the explicit residue coordinates; L2/L3 describe the same replacement in the mouse knock-in allele; L4/L5 confirm luminal surface display in mouse capillaries; L6/L7 confirm surface display in CHO cells. No other insertion positions (N-terminal, C-terminal, or in any other loop) are named or implied by any ledger line. The ledger does not support a separate N-terminal tag site: no clip describes a tag placed before residue 21 or after the signal-peptide cleavage site independently of the acidic-domain replacement. Validation is classified surface_only because LPL-binding function of the S-tagged construct is not explicitly reported in the provided clips; the clips do not state that LPL binding was measured and preserved for S-GPIHBP1 specifically.
